question: Do the update/package owners approve local packaged `dist` preservation and opt-in replay, including this exact legacy content-inventory exception set, as supported upgrade behavior?
rationale: Repeated technical reviews and real-filesystem proof are clean, but the PR deliberately creates a new executable-package mutation and upgrade compatibility contract that automation cannot accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Approve current guarded contract
options.body: Accept preservation by default and explicit trusted replay with the current integrity, topology, rollback, and compatibility guards.

options.title: Ship recovery-only
options.body: Keep capture and recovery reporting but remove automatic replay to avoid owning executable package mutation.

options.title: Decline packaged overrides
options.body: Keep installed package artifacts immutable and direct customization to source-managed workflows.

recommendation.title: Approve current guarded contract
recommendation.body: Accept preservation by default and explicit trusted replay with the current integrity, topology, rollback, and compatibility guards.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored or merged multiple recent package-update transaction changes and are the strongest available owner for the final policy choice.
